source_location: Table 3 'Bland-Altman statistics' (TST, WASO bias and LoA, N1 sleep-onset criterion); Table 4 'Epoch-by-epoch analysis' WASO row (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, MCC); Methods 'Statistical Analysis' for definitions; Methods 'Polysomnographic Recordings' for sample
notes: Bias sign flipped: paper reports PSG minus Fitbit (TST -4.0, LoA -204.3 to 196.3; WASO -37.1); values here are DEVICE minus PSG (TST +4.0, LoA -196.3 to +204.3; WASO +37.1). WASO LoA as printed in Table 3 are '188.1' and '113.8' (lower limit lacks a minus sign, almost certainly a typo for -188.1); after sign flip reported as -113.8 / +188.1 on the assumption the printed lower LoA is -188.1. LoA = bias +/- 1.96 SD; SD of differences and 95% CI of bias not tabulated (P values only; 95% CI of LoA shown graphically in Figure 5). Bland-Altman values are for N1-defined sleep onset and after manual removal of Fitbit 'bordering wake' epochs at sleep onset/offset; unadjusted values in Table S1 and N2-onset values in Table S2 (Multimedia Appendix, not accessed). One night per participant (baseline night; adaptation night used for 8 participants), ambulatory PSG at home. EBE: PSG scored in 20-s epochs, Fitbit 30-s stages; each PSG epoch compared with the dominating (>50%) Fitbit stage in the same interval; pooled across all epochs. Sensitivity here is for the WASO (wake) class: TP = wake epochs correctly detected; specificity = proportion of non-wake (sleep) epochs correctly identified as not wake. Values are proportions in the paper, converted to percent. Internal inconsistency in paper: Results text states accuracy for WASO 0.898, whereas Table 4 and Abstract give 0.824/0.82 (Table value used). No kappa, PABAK, F1 or AUC reported. Sleep efficiency not reported. SOL not reported (Table 3 gives sleep onset clock time bias -1.6 min PSG-Fitbit, LoA -68.8/65.6, not a latency); left null.

notes: Manufacturer white paper, not peer reviewed; algorithm shipped for Fitbit and Pixel watches in early 2026. Sensitivity = mean per-night sleep recall 0.95 (SD 0.08) and specificity = mean per-night wake recall 0.69 (SD 0.21), read from the Figure 5 binary confusion matrix (two decimals). TST bias and LoA read from the legend of the Figure 7 TST Bland-Altman panel (predicted minus ground truth, so already device minus PSG); the Awake-duration panel shows the mirror image (-2.17 min, LoA -72.96 to 68.62). Awake duration in Figure 7 is total wake within the scored window, not WASO, so not entered.
